items.content_text: With Black Friday deals in full swing, there aren't a lot of great TCG deals catching our eye yet. items.excerpt: RGB Mini-LED tech boasts richer colors, a brighter picture, and wider viewing angles than ever before.
items.content_text: Last year, Hisense pioneered the first RGB Mini-LED TV with its 116UX model. Granted it was only available as a massive 116" screen that retailed for $20,000. In 2026, Hisense released its second generation RGB Mini-LED tech at a much more affordable price point with its UR-series lineup. For Black Friday, you can get it for even less. Best Buy has just discounted the 65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV from $2,000 all the way down to $899.99 and the 75" model from $2,500 down to $1399.99, both with free delivery. These are the lowest prices since launch and beats previous lows by $200. The Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV Gives OLED a Run for Its Money RGB Mini-LED is essentially the next generation evolution of Mini-LED technology. Traditional mini-LED TVs consist of an array of blue LED that are passed through RGB filters to produced the desired color. RGB Mini-LED TVs use red, green, and blue LEDs instead of just blue, which means the pixels no longer need filters to produce the desired color. The result is more accurate color reproduction, less blooming and, most importantly, a wider color gamut. In fact, the color gamut of RGB Mini-LED surpasses that of OLEDs, since current-generation OLEDs also use color filters combined with blue OLEDs. How does that translate in the real world? It means that you see richer, more accurate colors, smoother gradients and less banding than even OLEDs, especially in 4K HDR content. RGB Mini-LED TVs have several other features that out-class standard Mini-LEDs. They're brighter (far brighter than OLED TVs), making them perfect for daytime watching in bright rooms with little light control. They offer much better viewing angles, which means everyone you're hosting will enjoy the game wherever they're positioned around the TV. Gamers will benefit from this TV as well. The Hisense UR8 boasts a 180Hz native refresh rate, the highest I've ever seen for a TV, with HDMI 2.1 inputs that will pair seamlessly with a PlayStation 5 console for seamlessly running games in 4K. items.title: GTA 6 Was Biggest Launch in PlayStation History
items.excerpt: Now that the dust has somewhat settled after the avalanche that was the launch of GTA 6, PlayStation has revealed some of its stats from the game, revealing that this was the single largest game release in PlayStation history.
items.content_text: Now that the dust has somewhat settled after the avalanche that was the launch of GTA 6, PlayStation has revealed some of its stats from the game, revealing that this was the single largest game release in PlayStation history. PlayStation’s November 23 blog post states that more than 39 million unique players have played the game on the PlayStation 5, setting a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any PlayStation game. This beats out other records for multiplayer games, single-player games, and perhaps most astonishingly, even free-to-play titles. On top of that, GTA 6 players logged a total of 683 million hours played in the game, with the average player spending an estimated 17.4 hours sticking up virtual pawn shops and stealing NPC’s cars during its first few days. What’s more impressive is the sheer amount of people who purchased PS5s specifically to play GTA 6. PlayStation’s blog says it saw the “largest number of newly-connected PS5 consoles on a single day” since the console’s launch in November 2020, not counting end-of-year holidays like Christmas. Since GTA 6’s launch, it was the first game played on 70% of these new consoles. GTA 6 has, perhaps unsurprisingly, broken a slew of big records. The most prominent of these is its status as the biggest entertainment launch of all time, with Rockstar reporting that the game earned $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours. On top of this, internet provider Comcast said that GTA 6’s launch day was its highest-traffic day ever , with 24% of all its internet traffic during peak times coming from users downloading and playing Rockstar’s latest offering. Xbox had its own big records, too; Xfinity, which is under the Comcast umbrella, said GTA 6 increased the internet traffic on Xbox consoles by four times the normal amount this November. People are still making new discoveries in this game, and there’s bound to be many more that pop up over the next few months. GTA 6 is up for eight awards at The Game Awards and has enjoyed massive critical reception, with IGN scoring it a glowing 10 out of 10 — the title of ‘Masterpiece.’ Reviewer Luke Reilly praised the game for being “exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered,” saying “Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played.” It’s unlikely that we see a game release as big as this one, with such a massive cultural impact, ever again. Rockstar certainly set a new standard for the industry with this one, to the point where many users aren’t sure if a photo they see online is from the real world or from the game . items.title: Call of Duty's Player Count Dropped by Over 40% Following GTA 6's Release, According to Analysts
items.excerpt: A new report claims that Call of Duty saw an over 40% drop in players following GTA 6's release.
items.content_text: A new report claims that Call of Duty saw an over 40% drop in players following GTA 6's release. We've known all year long that Rockstar Games was going to dominate the final two months of 2026 thanks to the release of GTA 6. It's why a lot of publishers moved their games either into 2027 or pushed them up to September to steer clear of the blast radius. Call of Duty, however, releases on an annual cycle around October or November, which means Modern Warfare 4's post-launch plans were beginning right around the time of GTA 6's launch. According to Alinea Analytics, it appears that Call of Duty lost almost half of its player base during GTA 6's record-breaking launch weekend . The Call of Duty app (which consists of Warzone, Black Ops 7, and Modern Warfare 4) saw a 42% drop across platforms, taking the overall daily player count from 7.6 million users to 4.4 million users. There's likely a lot of crossover between GTA and Call of Duty's audiences, so it's no surprise to see a drop in players, but nearly half clearly highlights just how much of an event GTA 6 is. Call of Duty app (MW4, Warzone, and BO7) lost 42% of players following GTA 6's launch, down from 7.6M daily active users to 4.4M PS5 saw the biggest drop off out of all platforms with 44% decline in players, per Alinea Analytics https://t.co/cARXye3Ahs — CharlieIntel (@charlieINTEL) November 23, 2026 Earlier this fall, Activision chief marketing officer Tyler Bahl stated that he believed GTA 6 would actually help Call of Duty , as the open-world crime epic would drive more attention toward gaming as a whole. People are buying new consoles or dusting off old ones to play this game, so in theory, they will turn their attention toward other titles once they are done with GTA. Whether that title is Call of Duty remains to be seen, but currently, it appears to only be hurting the series in the immediate short term. Things will probably bounce back up, but it'll be interesting to see how many people return. This also may not be the last time Call of Duty takes a hit from GTA 6. There are expected to be at least two more big beats or launches for this game, with the PC release rumored for an early 2027 release . However, the even bigger moment will come in the form in the inevitable online mode. Rockstar hasn't talked about its plans for GTA 6's online offerings yet, but it's highly speculated to release sometime next year . If it drops in the summer, it may not hurt Call of Duty a ton since that is the period where the most hardcore fans are still grinding away on the game. But if GTA 6 Online dropped next fall, around October or November, it could put Call of Duty in a really difficult position. It'll be an interesting story to follow, but Call of Duty has been battling intense competition for two straight years now thanks to Battlefield 6 in 2025 and GTA 6 this year. Maybe it can contend next year, but the jury is still out.
items.title_en: Call of Duty's Player Count Dropped by Over 40% Following GTA 6's Release, According to Analysts

items.title: Ted Lasso Renewed for Season 5 on Apple TV
items.excerpt: Ted Lasso is coming back to Apple TV for a fifth season, with production set to begin in April 2027.
items.content_text: Ted Lasso is coming back to Apple TV for a fifth season, with production set to begin in April 2027. Apple TV’s beloved comedy series is coming back for another season, and it’s possible that there’s more in store. As pointed out by Variety , Jackson Sudeikis — who will return as both executive producer and star of the show — said he “would like to” continue the project through a sixth season in an October episode of Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso. “Yeah, I just don’t know,” he told the host when asked about the topic, clarifying that he wasn’t holding anything back “intentionally.” “We haven’t started a writers’ room or anything like that,” he added. For now, we know that Season 5 is in the bag, but this isn’t a huge surprise. In fact, it was almost a given, seeing how Season 4 was Apple TV’s biggest launch in the platform’s history. Its premiere garnered an astonishing 296.6 million minutes watched , proving the audience’s interest even after its initial storyline wrapped up at the end of Season 3. Now, Ted’s on a new mission: to coach a women’s football team. The newly formed second-division team, the Lady Greyhounds, take Ted on a parallel journey with new obstacles, primarily navigating the environment of women’s athletics and the unique challenges that come with it. Ted Lasso has been a hugely successful show, both among fans and critics alike. We at IGN scored its first season a glowing 9 out of 10 , calling it a “relentlessly optimistic and disarmingly charming comedy” that was sorely needed when it was released back in 2020. And while our review of the Season 4 premiere was comparatively softer , it certainly resonated with audiences enough to warrant a continuation of its new storyline. For those who are unfamiliar with the show, it follows the kind, optimistic Ted Lasso, an American college football coach who gets hired to help a struggling English football league whose owner secretly hopes it fails. It’s a delightful watch, and a premise that has continued to prove sorely sought-after in the six years since its initial release. Ted Lasso streams exclusively on Apple TV . For more shows streaming on the service, you can check out every series that’s making its way to the platform this November , which includes movies and shows like 12 12 12, Way of the Warrior Kid, and Stick Season 2.

items.excerpt: GTA 6 players are convinced that Rockstar Games painted a fake tunnel in Vice City just to trick them into ramming into it in a Looney Tunes-style crash.
items.content_text: GTA 6 players are convinced that Rockstar Games painted a fake tunnel in Vice City just to trick them into ramming into it in a Looney Tunes-style crash. Picture it: One day, Lucia's driving through Vice City without a care in the world, when suddenly – wham! – she splats right into the wall. That's a story that's become all too common in the early days of GTA 6 thanks to a very silly (and very convincing) mural located in the game. If you've ever seen a Wile E. Coyote cartoon, you probably know where this is going. The idea is that the painting on the wall looks so lifelike that anyone not hyper-focused on the details thinks they can drive straight through it like any other tunnel. While the trick typically works out for the Road Runner, Jason, Lucia, and the rest of the internet haven't been so lucky. Many 'GTA 6' fans are getting fed up after crashing into a painted wall because it looks like a real driving path 😂 https://t.co/1aUiG7qiON — internet hall of fame (@InternetH0F) November 23, 2026 Ludwig Drives Straight Into a Painted Wall in GTA VI Clipped from ludwig's live stream Follow for the best GTA 6 moments every day! #GTA6 #ludwig #GTAVI https://t.co/sDE9kbneUq — ChatSaidClipThat (@ChatSaidClip) November 21, 2026 Let's be honest: Rockstar probably did this on purpose. These crashes and Looney Tunes comparisons are way, way too common for it to have been something the developers didn't consider. Maybe the team didn't expect that many people to fall for the gag, or maybe they expected more players to notice it before running face-first into the wall, but it's hilarious, either way. If there's anything we've learned from the early days of GTA 6, it's that Rockstar spent its lengthy development time well. Leonida is packed with things to do, people to meet, and secrets to discover, and even though so much has already been found after just one weekend, it's clear players won't be done anytime soon. items.title: GTA 6 Praised for Its Accurate Portrayal of Felon Rehabilitation
items.excerpt: GTA 6 is receiving praise for its commentary on how hard it is for felons to start a life and the system that breeds crime.
items.content_text: GTA 6 is receiving praise for its commentary on how hard it is for felons to start a new life and the system that breeds crime. In GTA 6, Jason and Lucia choose a life of crime in hopes of creating financial stability in their lives. Their goal isn't necessarily to get rich and buy flashy cars or a mansion, but so they can lay the foundation for their family. Although Jason runs drugs for a local crime boss, Lucia in particular is the one who really pushes them to take on more ambitious jobs. Some players felt that her decision-making at the start of the game was a bit reckless, given that she just got out of prison — but if you read her text messages, things begin to make a lot more sense. Players realized that her parole officer had denied her petition to take a job at a local bar, one of her only options for employment because she knew someone who worked there that could vouch for her. Without that, her record as a convicted felon would make it difficult for employers to consider her for a position. Her PO also noted that she's overdue on paying court-ordered parole fees, which she can't pay because she doesn't have a job, putting her in a vicious cycle. Lucia's willingness to get back into crime makes a lot more sense when you look at her texts with her PO and see that they denied her request to get a job but still wanted her to pay bills she has no money for https://t.co/HBfpsZEmz2 — Nikuo 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 (@MEATMAAAAN) November 23, 2026 This pushes Lucia to get involved with shady characters who turn her life with Jason upside down. A number of fans have praised this particular narrative beat, including some who have worked within this very system. "As someone who worked as part of the system years ago, not as a PO but a case manager, this is wildly accurate to real life," said X user Mgs2master . "Rockstar did their homework here." "GTA 6 is brave enough to try and educate the player on how desperation can drive you to crime through how it incorporates gameplay mechanics into the story," said one player . "It's genuinely one of the best uses of ludonarrative I’ve ever seen, period. I am floored." "As someone who's had family that has had to go through this s**t, it's genuinely not satirical," said another user . "This is straight up just what happens. The system is designed to funnel criminals back into crime by denying them opportunities needed to rehabilitate themselves to keep prisons full." Another person noted that this system blocks people out of having a reasonable chance of developing a good life: "The US has a recidivism problem because once you have a felony you're essentially locked out of a good chunk of employment and housing stuff, and then these orgs act surprised when people go back to crime. The econ equivalent of kicking people while they're down." Rockstar Games writer Rupert Humphries told Love Magazine earlier this year that the "American Dream" as we know it has scaled down for many people with each passing GTA game. Now, people just want a foundation to live and build a family, but the state of the world has made that increasingly unattainable, and in the case of GTA 6, it leads to the characters taking matters into their own hands. "Some would say the American Dream collapsed a long time ago," said Humphries. "With GTA 4, we told an immigrant’s story that was supposed to be a kind of hollow commentary on the illusion of America as a land of opportunity, and then we sort of doubled down on that with the cynicism of GTA 5. Maybe the American Dream is more modest now. It’s a house for your family and your loans paid off instead of wild success — but maybe today, that is just as out of reach for the average person. Miami and Southern Florida are a particular front line for this battle between astronomical wealth and unbounded ambition, creating a pressure cooker for all kinds of insanity." Of course, GTA 6 is still fiction and isn't an endorsement of real crime, despite how much some people would like you to believe otherwise . It's more so putting two charcaters in these circumstances and seeing how they react to the cards they're dealt. There also wouldn't be much of a game if Lucia decided to just spend the rest of her days scrounging for minimum wage work, after all. GTA 6 has been a roaring success so far, generating over $3.79 billion in revenue in its first 24 hours with over 32.5 million copies sold in pre-sales alone. The game is also a critical smash hit, tying with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the best reviewed video game in history on Metacritic. IGN gave GTA 6 a 10 out of 10 , praising it for its depth and detail. "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, GTA 6 has not stopped astonishing me since I started it," reads an excerpt from the review. "I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

items.content_text: GTA 5 's unstoppable train has been a meme for a decade, so naturally, players wasted no time trying to stop the one in GTA 6 – but they were sad to find out that it wasn't all that hard to do. What better way to spend the early days of a project that Rockstar Games fans waited 13 years for than to immediately do the same thing they've already been doing? As players were dropped into the south end of Leonida, many immediately took Jason as far as they could just to find a train to stand in front of. The iconic black, yellow, and white locomotive patrols Los Santos and has for years, and unlike just about every other vehicle in the game, there's nothing Michael, Franklin, or Trevor can do to stop it. Dumb trucks, C4, planes, rows of cars – you name it. No one has ever been able to get GTA 5's train to budge. After 13 years of trying, it's become a meme on the internet to try and move the train, resulting in countless videos that have cropped up from those seeking to test its mettle (and farm a bit of engagement on social media). Naturally, GTA 6 presented an updated take on the opportunity when players discovered its train. Unfortunately, Rockstar's commitment to realism means moving the new locomotive isn't just possible; it's actually kind of easy. Crash into it with a dump truck? Works like a charm. Park an excavator in its path? Stops it in its tracks. Raise a bridge? Completely detailed. Rockstar's new, smarter NPCs even have the brains to pull the brakes when they see a person simply standing in their way. This is where we get into the argument that has plagued Rockstar both inside and outside of the studio for years: When is a game too realistic? Judging by GTA 6's record-breaking earnings and all-time great reviews , it seems the developers' new playground struck a nice balance between being grounded and goofy. Of course, that hasn't stopped a small section of players from being upset that Leonida plays by many of the same rules that we do in the real world. After GTA 5's train spent more than a decade as the running champ of viral videos to come out of Los Santos, players aren't ready to let GTA 5's train go. items.title: The Rushed Rings of Power Episode Release Schedule Is Likely Thanks to Amazon's Black Friday Sale Strategy
items.content_text: Prime Video's The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 wraps up this Wednesday with its final two episodes. It's a surprisingly condensed release schedule for a billion-dollar TV series. Both Seasons 1 and 2 of the series were extended into more strung-out episode drops, so why is Amazon seemingly rushing this one? Well, while we don't have confirmation from Amazon directly, the answer seems to be pretty obvious: Black Friday . The Rings of Power is Amazon's biggest series and is presumably a significant draw to get people to sign up for an Amazon Prime membership just in time for the biggest shopping holiday of the year. The Rings of Power episode release schedules at a glance Season 1 - September 1 - October 14 (7 weeks) Season 2 - August 19 - October 3 (6 weeks) Season 3 - November 11 - 25 (3 weeks) 2026 marks the first time new episodes of The Rings of Power started dropping in November, as both previous seasons kicked off near the beginning of September. If you consider this change in release timing in terms of Amazon's eCommerce business, the reason for this seems rooted in the service's free trial . New subscribers can get an Amazon Prime membership for free for 30 days, and both the premiere and the finale of the Prime Video LOTR show fit neatly in that window. There's certainly nothing wrong with Amazon manipulating its Prime Video release schedule to aid the retail part of its business, assuming that is what is happening here. After all, the main draw of an Amazon Prime membership is that you get a streaming service and all of the Prime shopping benefits that come with it. The fact that Amazon is choosing to do this for the first time with Season 3 is what makes it so interesting. Prime Video is one of the biggest streaming services out there right now, but it's been a part of their service since 2011. While you can actually get a Prime Video subscription without getting an Amazon Prime membership, the free trial is only available for the full shopping subscription. So it's these big original shows like Rings of Power and Fallout that most likely drive high rates of free trial sign-ups to the service every year. For the folks who are only grabbing the free trial to watch the show and then cancelling after binge-watching, however, there's only a small window of time in which Amazon has to convince them to continue on with their subscription. With the streaming services becoming more and more expensive every year, this shift in Amazon's release schedule feels like a big deal. I myself have cancelled and renewed several streaming subscriptions this year based on the new shows coming out. I have very little time to watch TV in my week, so it's become harder for me to justify paying a monthly fee for something I'm not actively using. Amazon appears to be making an effort to adjust to this sort of mentality by aligning the rest of its subscription benefits with its biggest TV release of the year. We won't see how well this strategy works out for them this year until Amazon reveals its Q4 revenue numbers, but I have a feeling this is only the beginning of a much larger shift in streaming service strategy moving forward.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Will Have to Testify Publicly Before US Senate
items.excerpt: Earlier today, Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, after two weeks of scandals involving multiple affairs and a suspected spy. But while he's back in the pilot's seat, Huang's problems aren't over, and he's been summoned to testify in front of the US Senate.
items.content_text: Earlier today, Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO , after two weeks of scandals involving multiple affairs and a suspected spy. Although he's back in the pilot's seat, Huang's problems aren't over, as he's been summoned to testify in front of the U.S. Senate. Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify in front of the Senate's Banking Committee on December 3, according to Bloomberg . The hearing was announced by the committee's chairman, Tim Scott, and will focus on oversight of U.S. export controls. That comes just a week after Nvidia announced that it would be establishing a National Security and Export Control Committee last week . Huang's appearance in front of the Banking Committee is only the latest hearing that's been announced. Huang is also scheduled to appear in front of three House committees in two closed-doors meetings on December 1 and December 2 . While those congressional hearings will be closed to the public, they will be transcribed, and will likely also be covering Nvidia's adherance to U.S. export controls. But while Huang will now have to testify in front of both houses of Congress, his reinstatement came after President Donald Trump intervened on his behalf . In Nvidia's own statement about the CEO's return, it said, "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk." It turns out that input came from President Trump, who called the board and gave "reassurances" that Huang's return wouldn't pose a national security risk. While the President acted to have Huang reinstated, plenty of representatives from both parties have demanded answers on social media. Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren posted , saying, "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and NVIDIA still owe Congress answers. The Trump Administration needs to explain what 'input' was given and by which senior officials to support Huang’s reinstatement." At the same time, Republican Senator John Curtis posted, "Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior U.S. officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk. I have some questions. Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?" While this scandal built up steam in the background for months, it really exploded two weeks ago, when Huang admitted to an affair that kicked off an internal investigation into his conduct . He resigned just a few days later , and even though the board came out and said Huang wouldn't be reinstated , he reclaimed his office earlier today. Photo by Nadja Wohlleben/Getty Images.
